Exploratory. Three reference models stand for different accounts of what
drives children's arrangements: appearance without language (DINOv2),
appearance shaped by language (CLIP), and conceptual structure with no image
input (SPoSE).

The claim this part supports best is the within-child ranking — which
reference fits a given child better. Both correlations carry the same
attenuation, so it cancels exactly and no correction is needed. Correlations
compared *across* ages carry the same confound as Part 2 and are treated with
the same caution.

```{r}
#| label: setup
# Configuration and shared functions. setup.R is the single source of truth
# for every constant and helper used below.
source(here::here("setup.R"))
library(lme4); library(lmerTest); library(emmeans); library(broom)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

S <- readRDS("analysis_sample.rds")
fp <- S$children; cons <- S$consistency
str(S$config, max.level = 1)
```

# Load and verify the model RDMs

```{r}
#| label: load-rdms
rdms_raw <- read_csv(RDM_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE)
rdms_raw %>% count(domain, model, picture_set) %>% show_all()

# A child's vector averages trial 1 and trial 2, which used different
# photographs of the same concepts, so the model RDMs are averaged over
# picture sets too. SPoSE has no picture set: it is built from concepts.
model_rdms <- rdms_raw %>%
  mutate(picture_set = as.character(picture_set)) %>%
  group_by(domain, model, pair_index, concept_a, concept_b) %>%
  summarise(distance = if (any(picture_set == "avg")) {
              distance[picture_set == "avg"][1]
            } else {
              mean(distance)
            },
            n_sets = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(domain, pair_index, concept_a, concept_b),
              names_from = model, values_from = distance) %>%
  arrange(domain, pair_index)

for (nm in c("perceptual", "hybrid", "conceptual")) {
  if (!nm %in% names(model_rdms)) model_rdms[[nm]] <- NA_real_
}

verify_pair_order(model_rdms)

model_rdms %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(pairs = n(),
            has_perceptual = sum(!is.na(perceptual)),
            has_hybrid = sum(!is.na(hybrid)),
            has_conceptual = sum(!is.na(conceptual)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: concept-check
concept_check <- fp %>%
  distinct(category, base_name) %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(child = list(sort(base_name)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  full_join(model_rdms %>%
              group_by(category = domain) %>%
              summarise(model = list(sort(unique(c(concept_a, concept_b)))),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "category") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(same = identical(child, model),
         only_child = paste(setdiff(child, model), collapse = ", "),
         only_model = paste(setdiff(model, child), collapse = ", ")) %>%
  ungroup()

concept_check %>% select(-child, -model) %>% show_all()

usable <- concept_check %>% filter(same, category %in% DOMAINS) %>%
  pull(category)
cat("Domains usable for the model comparison:",
    paste(usable, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Emotion words are not THINGS object concepts, so emotions has no
# conceptual reference and appears only in the vision-model results.
cat("Domains with a conceptual reference:",
    paste(intersect(usable, CONCEPTUAL_DOMAINS), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# How much the references overlap

Two references that agree with each other cannot be told apart by any
amount of child data. This bounds every comparison below.

```{r}
#| label: overlap
model_rdms %>%
  filter(domain %in% usable) %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(n_pairs = n(),
            perc_hybr = round(safe_cor(perceptual, hybrid, "spearman"), 2),
            perc_conc = round(safe_cor(perceptual, conceptual, "spearman"), 2),
            conc_hybr = round(safe_cor(conceptual, hybrid, "spearman"), 2),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  show_all()
```

# Per-child fit to each reference

```{r}
#| label: fits
refs_long <- model_rdms %>%
  filter(domain %in% usable) %>%
  arrange(domain, pair_index) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(perceptual, hybrid, conceptual),
               names_to = "model", values_to = "distance") %>%
  filter(!is.na(distance)) %>%
  group_by(domain, model) %>%
  summarise(ref = list(distance), .groups = "drop")

pdv <- participant_dist_vecs(fp) %>% filter(category %in% usable)

fits <- pdv %>%
  inner_join(refs_long, by = c("category" = "domain"),
             relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  mutate(r = map2_dbl(dvec, ref, ~ cor(.x, .y, method = "spearman"))) %>%
  select(participant_id, category, model, n_trials, r) %>%
  inner_join(S$age, by = "participant_id") %>%
  add_age_bins() %>%
  left_join(cons %>% select(participant_id, category,
                            reliability = consistency),
            by = c("participant_id", "category"))

fits %>%
  group_by(category, model) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_r = round(mean(r), 3), sd = round(sd(r), 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  arrange(category, model) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: permutation
# Does a fit beat chance at all? Shuffle concept labels, which preserves the
# child's spatial arrangement and the reference's structure but destroys the
# correspondence between them.
set.seed(42)

perm_p <- function(dvec, ref, concepts, n_perm = N_PERM) {
  obs <- cor(dvec, ref, method = "spearman")
  n <- length(concepts)
  null <- replicate(n_perm, {
    o <- sample(n)
    m <- matrix(0, n, n)
    m[lower.tri(m)] <- dvec
    m <- m + t(m)
    mp <- m[o, o]
    cor(mp[lower.tri(mp)], ref, method = "spearman")
  })
  mean(null >= obs)
}

perm_tbl <- pdv %>%
  inner_join(refs_long, by = c("category" = "domain"),
             relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  mutate(p = pmap_dbl(list(dvec, ref, concepts), perm_p)) %>%
  select(participant_id, category, model, p)

perm_tbl %>%
  group_by(category, model) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pct_above_chance = round(100 * mean(p < .05), 1),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  arrange(category, model) %>% show_all()
```

# Within-child ranking

The strongest comparison available here. For each child, is the conceptual
reference a better fit than the perceptual one? Both correlations carry the
same reliability factor, so the comparison is attenuation-free.

```{r}
#| label: ordering
wide <- fits %>%
  select(participant_id, category, age, age_bin, age_group, model, r) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = r) %>%
  filter(!is.na(perceptual))

ordering <- wide %>%
  filter(!is.na(conceptual)) %>%
  mutate(difference = conceptual - perceptual,
         conc_wins = conceptual > perceptual)

ordering %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            pct_conceptual_wins = round(100 * mean(conc_wins), 1),
            mean_difference = round(mean(difference), 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  show_all()

ordering %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  filter(n() >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(binom = map(data, ~ {
            b <- binom.test(sum(.x$conc_wins), nrow(.x))
            tibble(k = sum(.x$conc_wins), n = nrow(.x),
                   p_binom = signif(b$p.value, 3))
          }),
         wilcox = map_dbl(data,
                          ~ signif(wilcox.test(.x$difference)$p.value, 3))) %>%
  select(-data) %>% unnest(binom) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: ordering-model
# One model over all domains with a conceptual reference, child as a random
# effect so a child contributing several domains is not counted as several
# independent observations.
if (n_distinct(ordering$category) > 1) {
  m_ord <- lmer(difference ~ category + (1 | participant_id), data = ordering)
  print(emmeans(m_ord, ~ category))
} else {
  m_ord <- lm(difference ~ 1, data = ordering)
  tidy(m_ord) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
    show_all()
}
```

```{r}
#| label: ordering-age
# Does the winning reference change with age? The cancellation holds within
# an age band, so a shift in the ranking across bands is interpretable even
# though the raw fits are not comparable across ages.
ordering %>%
  group_by(category, age_bin) %>%
  filter(n() >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pct_conceptual_wins = round(100 * mean(conc_wins), 1),
            mean_difference = round(mean(difference), 3),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  arrange(category, age_bin) %>% show_all()

ordering %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(age_bin) >= 3) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(t = map(data, ~ tidy(lm(difference ~ age, data = .x)))) %>%
  select(-data) %>% unnest(t) %>% filter(term == "age") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ordering
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
ordering %>%
  mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(age, difference, colour = category)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = .45, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = .7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = PALETTE) +
  labs(x = "age (years)", y = "conceptual minus perceptual fit",
       title = "Which reference fits each child better",
       subtitle = "Above zero: the conceptual reference fits better")
```

# Variance shares

Commonality analysis between the perceptual and conceptual references.
Reported as the weakest result here: simulation showed the unique-variance
share is only partly free of attenuation, so it is not a safe basis for a
developmental claim.

```{r}
#| label: commonality
commonality <- function(rp, rk, rpk) {
  if (!all(is.finite(c(rp, rk, rpk))) || abs(rpk) >= 1) return(NULL)
  r2_full <- (rp^2 + rk^2 - 2 * rp * rk * rpk) / (1 - rpk^2)
  tibble(r2_full = r2_full,
         unique_p = r2_full - rk^2,
         unique_k = r2_full - rp^2,
         shared = r2_full - (r2_full - rk^2) - (r2_full - rp^2))
}

ref_overlap <- model_rdms %>%
  filter(domain %in% usable) %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(rpk = safe_cor(perceptual, conceptual, "spearman"),
            .groups = "drop")

group_mean <- pdv %>%
  inner_join(S$age, by = "participant_id") %>%
  add_age_bins() %>%
  group_by(category, age_bin) %>%
  filter(n() >= MIN_BIN_N) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_vec = list(reduce(dvec, `+`) / length(dvec)),
            .groups = "drop")

shares <- group_mean %>%
  inner_join(model_rdms %>%
               filter(domain %in% usable) %>%
               arrange(domain, pair_index) %>%
               group_by(domain) %>%
               summarise(perc = list(perceptual),
                         conc = list(conceptual), .groups = "drop"),
             by = c("category" = "domain")) %>%
  inner_join(ref_overlap, by = c("category" = "domain")) %>%
  mutate(rp = map2_dbl(mean_vec, perc, ~ safe_cor(.x, .y, "spearman")),
         rk = map2_dbl(mean_vec, conc, ~ safe_cor(.x, .y, "spearman")),
         parts = pmap(list(rp, rk, rpk), commonality)) %>%
  filter(map_lgl(parts, ~ !is.null(.x))) %>%
  unnest(parts) %>%
  mutate(conceptual_share = unique_k / (unique_p + unique_k),
         across(c(rp, rk, rpk, r2_full, unique_p, unique_k, shared,
                  conceptual_share), ~ round(.x, 3)))

shares %>%
  select(category, age_bin, n, rp, rk, rpk, r2_full,
         unique_p, unique_k, conceptual_share) %>%
  arrange(category, age_bin) %>% show_all()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-shares
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
if (nrow(shares)) {
  shares %>%
    mutate(category = fct_domain(category)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(age_bin, conceptual_share, colour = category)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = n)) + geom_line(linewidth = .7) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PALETTE) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 4)) +
    ylim(0, 1) +
    labs(x = "age band", y = "conceptual share of unique variance",
         title = "Conceptual versus perceptual unique variance",
         subtitle = "Exploratory: only partly free of attenuation")
}
```
